topicName: Backup, Disaster Recovery, and Configuration as Code (JCasC)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Backup, Disaster Recovery, and Configuration as Code (JCasC) in Jenkins"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Maintaining a reliable Jenkins environment requires robust backup strategies, clear disaster recovery protocols, and reproducible configurations. This tutorial covers setting up Jenkins Configuration as Code (JCasC) and implementing an automated backup strategy to safeguard your continuous integration infrastructure."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A running Jenkins instance (version 2.222.1 or newer recommended)."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Administrator access to Jenkins."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Basic familiarity with YAML syntax and Linux command line operations."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Installing Required Plugins"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"To implement Configuration as Code, you must install the Configuration as Code plugin along with the Backup/Restore plugin for state management. Navigate to Manage Jenkins -> Manage Plugins and install the following:"},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Configuration as Code Plugin (configuration-as-code)"},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Plugin First (plugin-first)"},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"ThinBackup (thin-backup)"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Defining Jenkins Configuration as Code (JCasC)"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"JCasC allows you to define your Jenkins settings using a human-readable YAML file. Create a file named jenkins.yaml on your server."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"jenkins:
  systemMessage: "Managed by Jenkins Configuration as Code (JCasC)"
  numExecutors: 4
  scmCheckoutRetryCount: 2
  mode: "NORMAL"
unclassified:
  location:
    url: "http://jenkins.example.com/"
security:
  apiToken:
    tokenGenerationEnabled: true"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Set the environment variable CASC_JENKINS_URL to point to this configuration file's path, or upload it directly through the Manage Jenkins -> Configuration as Code interface."},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Configuring Automated Backups with ThinBackup"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"While JCasC manages your configuration, job histories, builds, and plugins require a separate backup mechanism. ThinBackup lightweight plugin only backs up necessary configuration and build files rather than large workspace directories."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Go to Manage Jenkins -> ThinBackup."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Click Settings."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Define the Backup directory path (e.g., /var/jenkins_home/backups)."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Set a Cron schedule for full backups (e.g., H 2 * * * for daily backups at 2 AM)."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Check the boxes for 'Backup plugin installations' and 'Backup global configuration'."},{"order":23,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 4: Disaster Recovery Plan"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"In the event of a catastrophic infrastructure failure, execute the following disaster recovery steps to restore Jenkins to its previous state:"},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Provision a new virtual machine or container running the same version of Jenkins."},{"order":26,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Install the ThinBackup plugin and configure the backup directory to point to your secure remote storage containing the latest backup archives."},{"order":27,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Navigate to ThinBackup and select 'Restore', choosing the most recent restore point."},{"order":28,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Restart the Jenkins service to apply restored jobs, user data, and history."},{"order":29,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Apply your JCasC YAML file via version control integration to ensure global configurations match your pipeline expectations."},{"order":30,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":31,"type":"paragraph","text":"By combining Jenkins Configuration as Code (JCasC) for reproducible environments and ThinBackup for stateful data retention, you establish a resilient, auditable, and easily recoverable CI/CD platform."}]
